items.title: A Wearable Ultrasound Sensor for the Simultaneous Assessment of Hemodynamics and Blood Pressure.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains a major global health burden, and monitoring vascular information is crucial for the management of cardiovascular disease in daily life. However, existing wearable technologies suffer from limitations such as poor signal quality, limited sensing modalities, and low accuracy. Here, we propose a wearable ultrasonic array patch system comprising 64 elements to overcome the above difficulties and be used for tracking blood dynamics and blood pressure fluctuations. Guided by finite-element piezoelectric simulations, the size of the ultrasonic array was designed. Additionally, the patch utilizes a hydrogel material to ensure proper coupling with the skin. Testing revealed that the patch achieves a -6 dB bandwidth of 71% and a peak-to-peak received voltage of 0.22 V. The patch achieves a high spatial resolution of 0.96 mm × 0.60 mm at a detection depth of 15 mm. The system employs two key approaches to acquire physiological information. The first is a multimodal acquisition scheme capable of simultaneously capturing relative blood pressure trends and hemodynamic characteristics. The second is an angle-dependent reduced vector Doppler framework that utilizes multi-angle beams to calculate blood flow vectors. This work builds on existing wearable ultrasound devices and establishes a platform for the continuous assessment and monitoring of vascular hemodynamics.

items.title: Communication-focused interventions to reduce missed nursing care: A systematic review.
items.abstract: Missed nursing care (MNC) is associated with adverse patient outcomes, and communication problems may contribute to care omissions. Evidence on interventions that explicitly target communication to reduce MNC remains unclear. To synthesize interventional evidence on communication-focused strategies intended to reduce MNC or specific nursing care omissions. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of six databases and gray-literature sources. Randomized, quasi-experimental, and pre-experimental studies involving nursing staff in health institutions were eligible when communication was an explicit intervention component. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using design-appropriate tools and GRADE. Owing to heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively. Six U.S. studies met the inclusion criteria: four quasi-experimental, one pre-experimental, and one randomized intervention study. Interventions included structured handovers and care-plan communication, teamwork training, electronic communication systems, and cue-based strategies. Three studies directly measured MNC using MISSCARE; others assessed communication processes or downstream clinical outcomes. Selected care omissions or communication processes improved in some studies, but findings were inconsistent. Moderate-to-high risk of bias, imprecision, heterogeneous outcomes, and inconsistent reporting precluded meta-analysis and limited certainty. Communication-focused interventions may improve selected aspects of care completion or communication, but current evidence does not establish a consistent or generalizable effect on MNC. Stronger studies using standardized MNC outcomes are needed, particularly outside the United States. This review identifies a small and heterogeneous body of intervention evidence in which communication is explicitly targeted to reduce MNC or care omissions. Direct measures of MNC should be distinguished from communication processes, patient experience, and downstream clinical outcomes. Evidence from LMICs remains absent.

items.title: Reply: Microvascular Dysfunction and Residual Angina After PCI.
Reappraising Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in Patients With Cancer.
Decoding Atrial Fibrillation Heterogeneity: A Nationwide Phenome-Wide Association Study in England.
items.abstract: Age and sex influence atrial fibrillation (AF) prevalence and outcomes, yet comprehensive data on sex- and age-specific health care utilization in patients newly diagnosed with AF remain limited. We aimed to address this gap using a phenome-wide association study (Phe-WAS) approach. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using nationwide Clinical Practice Research Datalink data linked to Hospital Episodes Statistics. Adults diagnosed with AF between 1998 and 2016 (n = 199,433) were matched 1:1 by age and sex to non-AF control subjects. Primary and secondary care interactions 5 years post diagnosis were analyzed using Phe-WAS with Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds. Logistic regression estimated odds ratios for conditions in AF vs control groups, stratified by sex and age. Associations were assessed for novelty through literature review and causality using published Mendelian randomization studies. Patients with AF had higher rates of cardiovascular and noncardiovascular conditions than control subjects, with marked sex- and age-specific patterns. Women had more bleeding complications, pneumonia, Clostridium difficile enterocolitis, cholangitis, and electrolyte disturbances, whereas men had higher rates of alcohol-related disorders, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, and cardiomyopathy. Younger patients with AF ( 60 years) more often had heart failure, ischemic stroke, renal failure, and respiratory infections. Of 51 phenotypes more common in AF, 28 were previously reported, and 23 were potentially novel. Mendelian randomization analyses suggested AF was causal for 19 associations. This Phe-WAS demonstrates the broad spectrum of health care interactions in AF beyond traditional cardiovascular complications.

items.title: A Biocompatible Cu(I)-Catalyzed Click Chemistry Framework for Long-Term Cell Tracking.
items.abstract: Cellular immunotherapies have transformed oncologic treatment in recent years, yet the inability to monitor cell migration post-transfusion remains a significant barrier to their development. Here, we explore the feasibility of a non-invasive cell-tracking method utilizing Cu(I)-catalyzed click chemistry in which cells are first labeled with alkynes and, after 1-2 weeks, are selectively targeted via an azide-conjugated fluorescent probe. We developed Click1, a novel tris-Cu-chelating azide capable of a rapid, robust click reaction directly on live cell surfaces with minimal cytotoxicity. When paired with Click1, two distinct alkyne-labeling reagents, N-(4-pentynoyl)-mannosamine-tetraacylated (Ac4ManNAl) and propargyl choline, were capable of detecting human T cells for over two weeks. Our findings elucidate the metabolic turnover of biochemical handles in primary immune cells, providing a potential framework for long-term cell tracking in immunotherapies.

items.title: A Multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program for the Evaluation and Management of Patients With SLE and Cognitive Concerns.
items.abstract: To develop and implement a standardized, comprehensive multidisciplinary program for the evaluation and management of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and cognitive concerns that would lead to improved diagnosis and management. The Neuro-Lupus Program evaluated 50 patients with SLE referred for any neurocognitive concern over a 12-month period. A specific sequential work-up protocol was developed for standardized patient evaluation. Initial history and examination were performed by a dedicated lupus neurologist followed by referral for comprehensive neurocognitive testing. Patients with suspected mood or psychotic disorders were evaluated in a specialized autoimmune psychiatry clinic. MRI brain scans were performed in all patients. Patients with MRI evidence of inflammation or cognitive impairment were further assessed with CSF studies and FDG-PET/CT brain. Management of neuropsychiatric medications and immunotherapy was a collaboration between neurology, psychiatry, and rheumatology. Full neurocognitive evaluation revealed a previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in 46.4% of patients tested (mild 39.3%, major 7.1%), with an additional 39.3% demonstrating a normal cognitive profile with isolated weakness. MRI demonstrated white matter disease in 50% of patients and cerebral atrophy in 10%. Brain FDG-PET/CT was performed in 8 patients (16%), 7 (88%) of which were abnormal. CSF studies demonstrated normal protein and white cell counts, but 25% had elevated kappa free light chains. As a result of this program, neuropsychiatric medications were optimized in 86% of patients and 8% had an escalation in immunotherapy. This multidisciplinary Neuro-Lupus Program model brings together neurologists, psychiatrists, rheumatologists, and neuropsychologists to standardize the approach to neurocognitive symptoms in SLE. Among the patients enrolled, this program detected previously undiagnosed cognitive impairment in the majority of those tested and was associated with changes in neuropsychiatric and immunotherapy management.

items.title: Incidence and clinical impact of venous thromboembolism during immunotherapy for gynecologic cancer.
items.abstract: To evaluate the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes associated with venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with gynecologic cancer treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). This retrospective cohort study included patients with gynecologic malignancies treated with ICI at a single institution between January 2017 and April 2026. The primary outcome was the development of VTE from ICI initiation through one month after the final cycle. Incidence, clinical characteristics, risk factors, and healthcare utilization were evaluated. Among 458 patients who received ICI therapy, 37 (8.1%) experienced a VTE. Deep vein thrombosis was the most common event (48.6%, n = 18), followed by pulmonary embolism (40.5%, n = 15). The median time from ICI initiation to VTE was 1.43 months (IQR, 0.70-2.93). Endometrial cancer was the most common disease site among patients with VTE (54.1%, n = 20). Smoking history differed significantly between groups (p < 0.01). ICI monotherapy was more common among patients who experienced VTE compared with those who did not (64.9% vs. 44.9%, p = 0.020), and patients with VTE had received fewer total lines of therapy (2.4 vs. 3.3, p = 0.008). Most events required emergency department evaluation (64.9%, n = 24) and hospitalization (59.5%, n = 22), and ICI therapy was delayed in 24.3% (n = 9) of cases. Breakthrough thrombosis was observed in 18.9% (n = 7) of patients receiving anticoagulation. VTE occurred in 8.1% of gynecologic cancer patients receiving ICI, was early in onset, and carried significant clinical burden. These data can guide provider awareness and patient counseling when initiating ICI in this population.

items.title: Outcomes of CD20-targeting CAR T-cell therapy in patients with advanced melanoma: MB-CART20.1 Melanoma phase I trial.
items.abstract: Previous studies identified CD20 + cells within the melanoma tumor microenvironment, including tumor-associated B-cells and putative cancer stem cells (CSC), as potential therapeutic targets. We therefore evaluated CD20-targeting CAR T-cells in patients with advanced melanoma. This prospective, open-label phase I trial evaluated a 3 +3 design in patients with advanced melanoma, refractory to approved treatments, to assess safety and preliminary activity of autologous anti-CD20 CAR T-cells (MB-CART20.1). Following lymphodepleting chemotherapy, patients received a single MB-CART20.1 infusion. Primary endpoints were safety and tolerability; secondary endpoints included kinetics and early evidence for antitumor activity. Three patients received dose level 1 (DL1) (1.0 ×10⁵ cells/kg) and four patients DL2 (1.0 ×10⁶ cells/kg). No DLTs occurred at DL1, while two patients experienced DLTs at DL2 (grade 3 ICANS and grade 4 hepatotoxicity). Overall, 43 serious TEAEs were reported across all seven patients. Stable disease was observed in three patients at week 16; all had progressed by month 6. All had received immune checkpoint inhibitors within 6 months before leukapheresis and showed reduced exhaustion marker expression on CD8 + T-cells. In addition, the frequency of CD19 + CD24 + CD27 + B reg cells trended to associate with progressive disease and inversely correlate with toxicity. MB-CART20.1 showed robust in vivo expansion however, severe DLTs at DL2 without durable clinical benefit led to early trial termination. In advanced melanoma, MB-CART20.1 was associated with marked expansion and toxicity, suggesting that B reg depletion and the melanoma-typical treatment history might have driven distinct CAR T-associated immunotoxicities.

items.title: Treatment-associated factors potentially linked to relapse in pediatric MOG antibody-associated disease: An exploratory case series.
items.abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) is an inflammatory demyelination disorder primarily affecting children. Pediatric-onset MOGAD typically responds well to corticosteroids; however, predictors of relapse and optimal strategies for sustained remission remain unclear. To explore treatment-associated factors that may be related to relapse in pediatric MOGAD, we focused on remission timing, second-line therapy, and prednisolone (PSL) tapering. We retrospectively analyzed 11 pediatric MOGAD cases diagnosed between 2015 and 2023. The clinical presentation, treatment course, and relapse patterns, including remission timing, second-line therapy, and PSL tapering, were reviewed. Among the 11 pediatric patients (median age at onset: 9 years; median follow-up: 70 months), five (45.5%) experienced relapse. Delayed remission and absence of early transition to second-line therapy were observed in relapsing cases. A shorter duration of low-dose PSL tapering (median 16.5 vs 86 days) was also more frequently observed in relapsing cases. In one patient, serum MOG antibody titers rose prior to clinical relapse. These observations are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted with caution given the small sample size. These hypothesis-generating observations suggest that optimizing acute-phase treatment may be important in reducing the relapse risk in pediatric MOGAD. Escalation to second-line therapy may warrant consideration when improvement is inadequate within the first days of acute treatment (no response by day 3 or insufficient improvement by day 5). Early escalation and a more gradual PSL taper were more often observed among patients who remained relapse-free. However, prospective studies with larger cohorts are required to confirm these findings.

items.title: Nitrogen-Functionalized Amphilectane-Type Diterpenoids with Anti-HBV Activity from the Okinawan Marine Sponge Stylissa sp.
items.abstract: Current treatments for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection are constrained by adverse effects, drug resistance, and the need for long-term administration. Therefore, the development of safer and more effective therapeutic agents remains an important priority. In this study, two new amphilectane-type diterpenoids, 7-isocyanatoneoamphilecta-11,15-diene (1) and 7-isothiocyanatoneoamphilecta-11,15-diene (2), together with three known analogues (3-5), were isolated as anti-HBV agents from the Okinawan marine sponge Stylissa sp. The structures of 1 and 2 were elucidated by spectroscopic analysis, single-crystal X-ray diffraction, microcrystal electron diffraction (microED), and chemical derivatization. The previously reported amphilectanes 6 and 7 from an Adociidae sponge were also evaluated to examine structure-activity relationships. Compounds 3 and 6 showed the most potent anti-HBV activity and significantly suppressed the formation of HBV covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) without affecting HBV binding, entry, or RNA transcription. These results suggest that the combination of an isocyanide group and an exomethylene moiety is critical for activity. This study expands the chemical diversity of amphilectane diterpenoids and highlights their potential as promising scaffolds for the development of anti-HBV therapeutics.

items.title: Fiber-2 induces autolysosome dysfunction and impairs autophagic flux to promote FAdV-4 replication.
items.abstract: Fowl adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4) causes hepatitis-hydropericardium syndrome in poultry, yet viral subversion of host autophagy remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of the viral structural protein Fiber-2 in modulating the host autophagy-lysosome pathway. Transcriptomic profiling of LMH cells expressing Fiber-2 revealed coordinated upregulation of autophagy-related genes, validated by quantitative PCR. Functional assays demonstrated that Fiber-2 expression leads to autophagosome accumulation and impaired autophagic flux, as shown by LC3-II/p62 analysis, tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter imaging, Bafilomycin A1 treatment, and transmission electron microscopy. Fiber-2 predominantly localizes to late endosomes and lysosomes, and GFP-Galectin-3 reporter assays indicate that it disrupts lysosomal membrane integrity rather than blocking autophagosome-lysosome fusion. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and enrichment analyses identified BECN1, a key autophagy regulator, as a Fiber-2-interacting protein, and associated host proteins were enriched in autophagy-related pathways. Finally, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Fiber-2 significantly reduced FAdV-4 replication at later stages of infection, consistent with a proviral role for Fiber-2. These findings indicate that Fiber-2 disrupts autophagic flux by inducing lysosomal dysfunction and membrane damage, thereby promoting FAdV-4 replication and uncovering a previously unrecognized mechanism of viral subversion of host degradative pathways.

items.title: Genome-wide analysis of circulating fowl adenovirus E serotype 8b in poultry of Bangladesh.
items.abstract: Fowl adenoviruses (FAdVs), particularly serotype E (FAdV-E), pose a significant threat to commercial poultry worldwide by causing inclusion body hepatitis (IBH) and resulting in substantial economic losses. This study presents the first comprehensive whole-genome sequencing and characterization of three FAdV-E isolates (Alim_IBH_1006, Alim_IBH_1007, and Alim_IBH_1009) collected from IBH-affected commercial poultry in 2024. All genome assemblies were obtained using Illumina sequencing, with genome sizes of 43,686-44,092 bp in length and of GC content (58 %) at a range between 36 and 38 open reading frames (ORFs). These features are consistent with the structures of FAdV-8b (serotype E), which include distinctive inverted terminal repeats (ITRs). Nucleotide identities were 98.79 % to 99.23 % to a Malaysian FAdV-8b strain (UPM T27; PP153927) based on BLAST and pairwise analyses. The identification of the isolates with each other varied between 100.00 % and 96.74 % to 97.51 % with the FAdV-E reference (NC_014969.1), while those with non-E serotypes were much lower (≤78.66 %). Dot plot alignments supported extensive collinearity and conservation with the Malaysian reference, with most observed alterations explained as point mutations. The study conducted phylogenetic analyses of whole genomes, DNA polymerase, and hexon genes, confirming that the Bangladeshi isolates were within FAdV-E and clustered with 8b strains from Malaysia (UPM T27), China, and Peru, suggesting regional transboundary circulation. Using RDP4 for recombination analysis, a high number of significant events were detected between parental strains KU517714 and OL456208 (one large event at approximately 33,026-35,994 bp), and PQ179264/KU517714 are possibly involved in the evolution of FAdV-E by recombination. The results provide important baseline genomic information for FAdV-E serotype 8b in Bangladesh. While these local isolates highlight genomic features and recombination events, continuous large-scale nationwide surveillance across diverse poultry regions will be necessary to fully map the prevalence and genetic diversity of circulating strains.

items.title: Estimating progress on hepatitis C elimination targets among people in contact with drug services in Scotland: National retrospective cohort study.
items.abstract: Scotland's HCV elimination strategy has focused efforts on scaling up treatment in community-based settings, with population-based surveys indicating substantial reductions in HCV prevalence among people who inject drugs. We aimed to evaluate progress against World Health Organization (WHO) elimination targets using a national virtual cohort of individuals in contact with drug services in Scotland. The cohort was formed utilizing national administrative databases (including opioid agonist therapy prescribing, drug-related hospitalizations and specialist drug treatment) and linked to HCV databases to ascertain diagnosed infection status during January 2015-March 2024. Multi-state and logistic regression models were used to estimate undiagnosed infection among individuals not tested during follow-up. Among 78,444 individuals who attended drug services, 15,851 (20.2%) had died or migrated during follow-up. Among 62,593 remaining in the prevalent cohort, 12,553 had been diagnosed with HCV, with 86.8% treated. We estimated 2415 (95% CI 1827-3467) individuals had undiagnosed HCV; thus, 83.2% (77.0%-86.9%) of infection had been diagnosed. Prevalence decreased by an estimated 71.7% (66.0%-75.1%), accounting for estimated undiagnosed infection. During January 2015-March 2024, estimated (diagnosed and undiagnosed) HCV incidence was 1.73 (1.56-2.05) and 2.13 (1.97-2.46) per 100 person-years for the overall cohort and those with a recent opioid-related drug service attendance, respectively. Scotland has made significant progress towards HCV elimination targets, with high levels of diagnosis and treatment achieved among people in contact with a broad range of drug services. Further, we demonstrate that linkage of administrative data has an important role to play in evaluating progress on HCV elimination.
items.journal: The International journal on drug policy

items.title: Single-cell landscape of alcohol-related hepatitis reveals serum amyloid a hepatocytes as key drivers of disease pathogenesis.
items.abstract: Alcohol-related hepatitis (AH) is a severe form of alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). The cellular subpopulations that contribute to AH and dynamics remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify key cellular subpopulations and their interactions in AH and explore key mechanisms contributing to disease pathogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed starting from liver biopsies from patients with AH, early-stage ALD, and healthy individuals. Immunofluorescence was used to validate protein expression of selected markers. Liver biopsy-derived organoids were generated and exposed to a conditioned medium recapitulating AH (AH-medium) to assess serum amyloid A (SAA) secretion by ELISA. Circulating SAA levels were measured in plasma samples obtained from patients at different stages of ALD. Our analysis revealed an atlas of several cell subpopulations of AH, including hepatocytes expressing SAA, scar-associated (SA) endothelial cells, Fibulin-3+ mesenchymal cells, SA-macrophages expressing MMP19, activated CD4+ and stressed/effector CD8+ T cell subsets, and hyperactivated neutrophils expressing FPR2. Cell-communication analysis predicted a strong SAA-FPR2 interaction between hepatocyte and neutrophil subpopulations in AH. We confirmed that AH-hepatocytes secreted SAA in organoid cultures after stimulation with AH-medium. We also found out that circulating SAA levels were elevated in AH and were associated with reduced survival. The SAA-FPR2 pathway emerges as a potential mediator of inflammation in AH, offering potential therapeutic targets for this severe disease. This study provides new insights into the cellular heterogeneity and dynamics in ALD progression, dissecting AH at a single-cell level.

items.title: Sesquiterpenoid Dimers from the Roots of Two Species of the Genus Inula with Cytotoxic Activity on Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells.
items.abstract: Guided by the feature-based molecular networking approach, twenty-five previously undescribed sesquiterpenoid dimers (SDs) designated Inulaenoids A-Y (1-4, 8-25, and 27-29) along with four known analogues were isolated from the roots of Inula helenium L. and Inula racemosa Hook. f. Their structures and absolute configuration were unambiguously elucidated by spectroscopic data, X-ray diffraction, and theoretical calculations. Structurally, compounds 1-19 are rare SDs featuring two eudesmane units directly constructed through C-C bonds, including C-13-C-13', C-13-C-11', C-11-C-13', and through a previously undescribed C-13-C-8' connection. Fifteen compounds (3, 4, 10, 15-18, 20-23 and 25-28) showed potent cytotoxic activity to Huh-7 and HepG2 cells with the IC50 values ranging from 1.9 ± 0.1 to 20.2 ± 0.3 μM. Among them, four compounds (3, 4, 10 and 17) displayed binding to proto-oncogenic c-Fos. Notably, compound 17 exhibited the highest binding affinity to recombinant human c-Fos, thereby activating TP53 transcription and subsequently driving BAX/Bcl2-mediated apoptosis in liver cancer cells. Taken together, this study expands the structural diversity of sesquiterpenoid dimers from genus Inula as novel c-Fos-targeting lead compounds, providing new insights for the development of natural product-based anti-hepatocellular carcinoma agents.

items.title: Advances in microfluidic chip technologies for the study and management of gastrointestinal cancers.
items.abstract: Gastrointestinal cancers (GICs) remain a major global health burden due to late-stage diagnosis, limited therapeutic efficacy, and poor prognosis. Conventional diagnostic and treatment strategies are often invasive, costly, and lack real-time monitoring capabilities, highlighting the need for the innovative and patient-centered approaches. This review critically examines the recent advances in microfluidic chip technologies for the diagnosis, modeling, and treatment of GICs, including gastric, colorectal, liver, pancreatic, and esophageal cancers. Microfluidic platforms enable the precise manipulation of microscale fluids, offering advantages such as reduced reagent consumption, high sensitivity, and integration of multiplexed assays into portable systems. Notably, recent studies demonstrate diagnostic performance with area under the curve (AUC) values exceeding 0.90 and sensitivities approaching 90%, while detection limits for key biomarkers such as ctDNA and proteins have reached attomolar (10⁻¹⁸ M) and picogram-per-milliliter levels. Applications discussed include circulating tumor cell (CTC) isolation, exosome and ctDNA detection, tumor-on-chip models, and microfluidic drug delivery systems. In addition, advances in materials, fabrication techniques, and fluid dynamics are evaluated for their role in optimizing device performance. Emerging integrations with machine learning further enhance diagnostic accuracy and predictive capability. Despite these promising developments, challenges related to standardization, scalability, and clinical validation remain. Overall, microfluidic technologies represent a transformative platform for enabling rapid, minimally invasive, and highly sensitive approaches to cancer diagnosis and personalized therapy in gastrointestinal oncology.

items.title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification.
items.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is constrained by rapid RNA degradation during sample storage, necessitating cold-chain logistics. Here we present spatially confined biosilicification (SCB), wherein RNA is encapsulated within a nanoscopic layer of amorphous silicon dioxide, as a highly effective methodology enabling ambient-temperature preservation of single-cell transcriptomes. By judiciously incorporating a silicification inhibitor, SCB achieves spatiotemporal control over both intra- and extracellular silica deposition, preventing excessive crosslinking and cell aggregation while preserving RNA biointegrity and accessibility. scRNA-seq performed with biosilicified cells (Si-scRNA-seq) maintained high transcriptomic fidelity with fresh samples (R 2 = 0.95 after 7 d) extending RNA half-life to 54.8 d at 25 °C, a 685-fold improvement compared to unprotected samples. Furthermore, Si-scRNA-seq confers robust resistance against oxidative and UV degradation. Compatible with mainstream platforms at ~0.1 RMB per sample, Si-scRNA-seq successfully resolves cellular heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver, and ovarian cancer specimens after extended room-temperature storage. Si-scRNA-seq provides a scalable and cold-chain-free solution for single-cell transcriptomics in research and clinical settings.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

items.title: Polylactic co-glycolic acid (PLGA)-based nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract: A potential therapeutic strategy against oxidative stress and diabetes in rat model.
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia arising from insulin resistance or impaired insulin secretion. Conventional and commercially available effective antidiabetic drugs are often associated with adverse effects and reduced efficacy over prolonged use, highlighting the need for safer and plant-based alternatives. Persea americana seed extract (PSE) has antidiabetic potential but suffers from non-specific distribution and poor bioavailability, thus limiting its clinical application. This study developed and evaluated the poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles encapsulating Persea americana seed extract (PSENP) to enhance therapeutic efficacy and delivery. Nanoparticles were characterized for zeta size, zeta potential, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), stability and their phytochemical composition, with HPLC confirming the presence of bioactive compounds including quercetin, syringic acid, and gallic acid. In-vivo, forty wistar rats were allocated into five groups: normal control, diabetic control, metformin-treated, PSE-treated, and PSENP-treated. Biochemical parameters were evaluated including fasting blood glucose, insulin (serum level), lipid profile, oxidative stress biomarkers (superoxide dismutase, catalase), and inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α). Histopathological examination of pancreatic tissue and safety evaluations for kidney and liver were performed. Moreover, In-silico study demonstrated the strong binding affinity between quercetin and α-glucosidase, thus supporting the glucose-lowering role of quercetin. The PSENP administration resulted in statistically significant glycemic control, enhanced antioxidant activity of enzymes, improved lipid profile, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, and preservation of architecture of pancreas, with no renal and hepatic toxicity. The findings of the study indicated that PLGA-based nanoformulation of P. americana seed extract provides a promising therapeutic strategy for diabetes management and its oxidative and inflammatory complications.

items.title: AREG mediates transient hepatocellular carcinoma resistance to receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
items.abstract: Lenvatinib is a first-line therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet resistance remains a major clinical challenge. Emerging studies suggest resistance evolves through dynamic multi-step processes. Here, using multi-timepoint and multi-omics sampling, we characterized the trajectory of lenvatinib resistance in HCC cells and identified three adaptive states marked by state transitions. Multi-omics analyses and functional validation identified amphiregulin (AREG) as a key transient mediator of resistance in our models. AREG is a sufficient and dominant ligand to promote cell survival through epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) activation. Pharmacological inhibition of the AREG-EGFR axis specifically targeted early-resistant cells. Furthermore, AREG upregulation was validated in additional replicate experiments and another HCC cell line. Mechanistically, a focal deletion on chromosome 3p may contribute to NF-κB activation and AREG expression. This study delineates a recurrent yet transient adaptive mechanism and suggests new therapeutic opportunities-such as combination therapies targeting transient resistance mechanisms-to prevent or overcome drug resistance.
